title: KCSAN: data-race in mod_timer / run_timer_softirq
two_threads_summary: KCSAN-reported two-context race. KCSAN: data-race in mod_timer / run_timer_softirq
audit_notes: Subject: 'hrtimer: Annotate lockless access to timer->state'. Pre-classifier PROBABLY_GOOD (real synchronization primitives on + lines).
fix_commit_message:
56144737e67329c9aaed15f942d46a6302e2e3d8
hrtimer: Annotate lockless access to timer->state

syzbot reported various data-race caused by hrtimer_is_queued() reading
timer->state. A READ_ONCE() is required there to silence the warning.

Also add the corresponding WRITE_ONCE() when timer->state is set.

In remove_hrtimer() the hrtimer_is_queued() helper is open coded to avoid
loading timer->state twice.

diff --git a/include/linux/hrtimer.h b/include/linux/hrtimer.h
index 1b9a51a1bccb..1f98b52118f0 100644
--- a/include/linux/hrtimer.h
+++ b/include/linux/hrtimer.h
@@ -456,12 +456,18 @@ extern u64 hrtimer_next_event_without(const struct hrtimer *exclude);
 
 extern bool hrtimer_active(const struct hrtimer *timer);
 
-/*
- * Helper function to check, whether the timer is on one of the queues
+/**
+ * hrtimer_is_queued = check, whether the timer is on one of the queues
+ * @timer:	Timer to check
+ *
+ * Returns: True if the timer is queued, false otherwise
+ *
+ * The function can be used lockless, but it gives only a current snapshot.
  */
-static inline int hrtimer_is_queued(struct hrtimer *timer)
+static inline bool hrtimer_is_queued(struct hrtimer *timer)
 {
-	return timer->state & HRTIMER_STATE_ENQUEUED;
+	/* The READ_ONCE pairs with the update functions of timer->state */
+	return !!(READ_ONCE(timer->state) & HRTIMER_STATE_ENQUEUED);
 }

+	/* Pairs with the lockless read in hrtimer_is_queued() */

 }
